Proof in the paper: The XRD patterns (Figure 2a) show characteristic reflections of wurtzite ZnO, Ni(111) plane, and Ni–Zn alloy.
A gradual shift of Ni(111) diffraction toward lower 2θ angles was observed at higher Ni content (Figure 2b), indicating the incorporation of Zn atoms into the lattice of metallic Ni.

The surface structure analysis by Raman spectroscopy (Figure 2c,d) demonstrates the disruption of the ordered crystalline arrangement of surface ZnO due to the potential fluctuations of the Ni–Zn alloy disorder.
The morphology analysis by SEM (Figure S3) and HRTEM analysis indicate the formation of Ni and Ni–Zn alloy particles (Figure S4b–d).
The lattice spacing (0.194 nm) in the inset of the NiZn (110) plane was measured using a fast Fourier transform (Figure 3d), which accords well with the XRD results.
